subject: NovaEdge: packaging swap vs. volume rebate — request for price-match evidence
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elenatorres@novaedge.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novaedge.io
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: price match + packaging options against CloudFlow

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. We just completed a review of our current vendor CloudFlow and they sent a quote that materially undercuts list on some of the pieces we care about (model serving egress, pre-warmed capacity). I attached a short RFP summary and the CloudFlow line-item quote for reference.

Quick context: NovaEdge is evaluating either a) a volume-based rebate (multi-year commitment) that mirrors CloudFlow's headline effective rate, or b) a consolidated bundle that includes Reserved Dedicated capacity + on-prem connector licensing with a migration credit. We need your commercial and packaging recommendation to present to procurement next week.

What would help:
- A formal price-match comparison doc we can use in procurement (line-item delta + assumptions).
- A clear articulation of migration credits and any time-limited incentives.
- Any technical caveats that affect rollout effort (KV cache compatibility, sequence-length assumptions).

Can we get a short write-up by EOD Monday (21st)? Also happy to do a 30m call if that helps.

Attachments: RFP_Summary.pdf, CloudFlow_quote.xlsx

Best,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement, NovaEdge
elenatorres@novaedge.io
procurement@novaedge.io

From: markus_klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elenatorres@novaedge.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: price match + packaging options against CloudFlow

Elena —

Thanks for the packet. I pulled the numbers and sketched two defensible commercial paths we can present to procurement. High level:

Option A — Volume rebate (multi-year):
- Match CloudFlow headline effective rate for the first year through a tiered rebate tied to committed spend.
- Includes a one-time migration credit (applied as billing credit over 3 months).
- Requires a 24-month minimum commitment to achieve parity.

Option B — Bundle (Dedicated + On-prem connector):
- All-in monthly fee with Reserved Dedicated capacity and an on-prem connector license.
- Higher up-front MRR but lower variable token spend; includes extended support SLA for first 90 days.
- We can offer a phased migration credit and an integration credit for the connector.

Key differentiators to make explicit in the write-up: runtime latency SLO, KV cache portability, shared vs dedicated KV limits, and egress treatment during warm-up. There are also non-linear savings from our caching/batching on mixed workloads — I flagged it in the attached draft comparison.

I added Kimberly to loop in the technical delta; we can circulate a short two-page price-match memo and a line-by-line delta table Monday morning. If you prefer, propose three slots and I'll book time.

Draft attachments: pricing-delta-draft.xlsx (internal) — linking in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xQ-novaedge-econ
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/78912

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elenatorres@novaedge.io>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: price match + packaging options against CloudFlow

Elena / team —

Quick technical notes to include in the procurement memo so expectations are aligned:
- KV cache portability: CloudFlow's implementation uses a different prefix strategy; migration requires a short conversion job for high-cardinality prefixes (2-4 weeks depending on dataset).
- Quantization/throughput: If NovaEdge opts for aggressive int8 quantization to reduce token cost, we can preserve accuracy with small calibration; runtime performance improves ~18% on our benchmarks but adds a one-time vetting step.
- Connector scope: The on-prem connector we include in Option B supports SSO + VPC peering; operational runbook add-on is a separate line item.

Commercial ask: If we offer the tiered rebate in Option A, recommend we carve out a short rollback window (60 days after go-live) to protect both sides while migrations stabilize.

I'll fold these into the price-match memo and the delta table Markus mentioned. Markus — I'll also include an ops-hour estimate we can put in the appendix.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Elena Torres <elenatorres@novaedge.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novaedge.io
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: price match + packaging options against CloudFlow

Markus / Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. The two-path framing is exactly what procurement needs. Let's do a 30m sync tomorrow to walk the memo and the line-by-line delta; please include the pricing-delta-draft.xlsx and the ops-hour appendix.

Also: procurement asked for a compact "price match certificate" summarizing assumptions and the effective matched rates for the first 12 months — can you generate that as a standalone PDF? We will attach it to our vendor decision memo.

I've attached our ProcurementChecklist.docx with the items the legal team will require for redline turnaround.

Available slots: Tue 21 Sep 2026 11:00-11:30 PT, Tue 21 Sep 2026 15:00-15:30 PT. Either works.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement, NovaEdge
Attachments: ProcurementChecklist.docx
